title: Seed Extraction, Drying, Cleaning, and Storage in Hot Climates
summary: Learn how to properly extract your seeds using two proven methods (with or without fermentation), quickly dry them in the shade without scorching, clean out impurities, and store them away from humidity and weevils using local resources.

pages.title: From Ripe Fruit to Seed Treasure
pages.text:
Your seed-bearing vegetables have reached perfect maturity in the field!
It's time to harvest and release the seeds enclosed within the heart of the fruits.
In this module, you will learn how to extract, wash, dry, and store your seeds without losing their germinative power.
Follow the steps carefully to preserve this living treasure!
pages.illustration_description: Une belle table de travail en bois sous un préau ombragé : fruits mûrs colorés (tomates bien rouges, courge dorée, piments), couteau, cuillère, récipients d'eau claire et bocaux en verre.

pages.title: Two Main Families of Fruits: Wet and Dry
pages.text:
Depending on the type of vegetable, the extraction method changes:
1. **Dry fruits** (beans, cowpeas, corn, okra): the pods are left to dry directly on the plant before being shelled dry.
2. **Fleshy fruits** (tomatoes, cucumbers, squash, eggplants): the seeds are bathed in juice or pulp and must be cleaned with water.
Let's start with fleshy fruits!
pages.illustration_description:
Comparaison en deux groupes sur une table :
- Groupe 1 : Gousses de niébé et de haricot toutes sèches et craquantes.
- Groupe 2 : Tomates mûres juteuses et melon ouvert montrant les pépins humides.

pages.title: Extraction with Fermentation (for Tomato and Cucumber)
pages.text:
Each tomato and cucumber seed is encased in a small, slippery jelly-like sac.
This jelly prevents the seed from germinating as long as it is inside the fruit.
To remove this coating without harming the seed, **fermentation** is used.
Fermentation dissolves the jelly and destroys microscopic diseases attached to the seed's surface!
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan sur une graine de tomate entourée de sa capsule gélatineuse translucide, puis une flèche montrant la même graine débarrassée de sa gelée, nette et poilue.

pages.title: The 3 Steps of Fermentation
pages.text:
Here's how to do it easily:
1. Cut the fruit in half and squeeze the seeds with their juice into a glass jar.
2. Don't add too much water (just a spoon if the juice is too thick).
3. Cover the jar with a piece of thin cloth and tie it to prevent fruit flies from entering.
Let it rest in the shade in a warm place (between 25° and 30°C).
pages.illustration_description:
Schéma séquentiel en trois étapes :
- Étape 1 : Pressage des demi-tomates au-dessus d'un bocal en verre.
- Étape 2 : Le bocal contient le jus et les graines.
- Étape 3 : Tissu fin noué sur le bocal avec un élastique, placé sur une étagère à l'ombre.

pages.title: Beware of the duration under high heat!
pages.text:
⚠️ Caution! In our hot climates, fermentation happens very quickly:
- Within 24 to 48 hours, a thin white film appears on the surface.
- Stir once a day with a clean stick.
As soon as the seeds detach and fall to the bottom of the jar: rinse immediately!
If you wait too long, the seeds will germinate in the jar and will be lost!
pages.illustration_description:
Vue à travers le bocal en verre :
- En haut : fine pellicule blanche et débris flottants.
- Au fond : les bonnes graines propres tombées au fond.
Une horloge affiche : "24 à 48h maximum sous climat chaud ⚠️".

pages.title: Extraction Without Fermentation (Squash, Eggplant, Watermelon)
pages.text:
For squash, melons, watermelons, and eggplants, no fermentation is needed!
1. Open the ripe fruit in half.
2. Scoop out the seeds with a spoon or by hand.
3. Place them in a sieve and gently rub them under a stream of clean water to remove the pulp.
For eggplant, mash the pulp in a bucket of water: the seeds will sink to the bottom!
pages.illustration_description: Une personne passe les graines de courge sous l'eau dans une passoire en frottant avec les doigts pour détacher les filaments oranges. Les graines ressortent toutes blanches et propres.

pages.title: The Final Rinse with Clear Water
pages.text:
Whether after fermentation or a simple wash:
- Pour your seeds into a fine-mesh sieve or colander.
- Run plenty of clear water over them, stirring with your hand.
- Remove all pulp debris and skins.
Your seeds should be perfectly clean to the touch, with no slimy residue!
pages.illustration_description: Gros plan sur les mains du maraîcher rinçant une passoire pleine de graines sous un robinet ou une gourde d'eau propre. L'eau qui s'écoule est limpide.

pages.title: Golden Rule of Drying: NEVER in Direct Sunlight!
pages.text:
⚠️ Caution! This is where the life of your seed is determined:
Never dry your seeds in direct sunlight!
The scorching sun cooks the living embryo hidden inside the seed and destroys its germination power.
Always dry your seeds **in the shade**, in a very airy and ventilated place!
pages.illustration_description:
Panneau comparatif choc :
- À gauche (gros soleil brûlant avec croix rouge ❌) : graines noircies ou cuites sur une tôle au soleil.
- À droite (coche verte ✅) : graines étalées sous un abri ombragé et bien balayé par une brise légère.

pages.title: Ideal Supports for Rapid Drying
pages.text:
Spread your seeds in a single, very thin layer:
- On a fine sieve, a terracotta plate, or a clean woven tray.
- Do NOT dry on newspaper: seeds stick to the paper and tear off!
For small quantities, unbleached brown paper coffee filters are perfect because they absorb water without sticking to the seeds.
pages.illustration_description:
Deux bons supports illustrés :
1. Une claie tressée traditionnelle à mailles fines surélevée du sol.
2. Des filtres à café suspendus à une corde à linge avec des pinces sous un préau.

pages.title: The thumbnail test to check for dryness
pages.text:
How to tell if the seed is perfectly dry?
Perform the **thumbnail test**:
Take a large seed (squash, corn, or bean) and press firmly with the edge of your thumbnail.
- If your nail leaves a mark or sinks in: there's still water, continue drying!
- If the seed is hard as a rock and your nail slides off: it's ready for storage!
pages.illustration_description:
Zoom sur un doigt appuyant fermement l'ongle sur une graine de courge :
- Cas A : empreinte marquée (légende : "Encore humide ❌").
- Cas B : graine rigide, ongle qui glisse sans laisser de trace (légende : "Parfaitement sèche ✅").

pages.title: Seed Cleaning: The Winnowing Method
pages.text:
For threshed seeds (beans, corn, okra, onions):
It often leaves a lot of dust and dry pod pieces.
Choose a day with a light, steady breeze.
Slowly pour your seeds from one calabash to another placed on a clean mat on the ground.
The wind carries away the light chaff, and the heavy seeds fall straight into the basket!
pages.illustration_description:
Le geste traditionnel du vannage :
Une maraîchère debout verse une pluie de graines depuis une calebasse haute. La brise dévie les débris légers sur le côté, tandis que les belles graines denses retombent en ligne droite dans la bassine au sol.

pages.title: Water Flotation Sorting
pages.text:
For some seeds (such as **onion**, **leek**, or **dried tomato**):
You can immerse them in a bowl of cold water:
- Full, heavy, and fertile seeds sink to the bottom of the container.
- Empty, shriveled seeds and debris float to the surface.
Skim off everything that floats, then collect the good seeds from the bottom and re-dry them immediately!
pages.illustration_description:
Un bol transparent en verre rempli d'eau :
- À la surface flottent quelques cosses et graines creuses avec une cuillère qui les retire.
- Au fond reposent les graines noires et denses.
Mention : "Graines lourdes au fond = graines vivantes ✅".

pages.title: The Three Deadly Enemies of Seed Storage
pages.text:
Once your seeds are clean and dry, you must protect them from their three main enemies:
1. **Air humidity**: it causes seeds to mold and rot.
2. **Excessive heat**: it depletes the seed's energy reserves.
3. **Insect pests**: weevils and bruchids bore into seeds from the inside.
pages.illustration_description:
Trois vignettes d'alerte :
1. Goutte d'eau avec moisissure verte ⚠️
2. Thermomètre qui explose sous la canicule ⚠️
3. Charançon grignotant un grain de haricot ⚠️

pages.title: 100% Airtight Containers
pages.text:
NEVER leave your seeds in cloth bags or open cardboard boxes during the rainy season!
Use airtight containers that seal perfectly:
- Glass jars with a clean rubber seal.
- Thick plastic bottles with tightly screwed caps.
- Traditional gourds sealed with clay or wax.
Outside air must never be able to enter!
pages.illustration_description:
Trois contenants modèles bien fermés posés sur une étagère :
1. Bocal en verre à joint hermétique.
2. Bouteille plastique type soda bien lavée et vissée à fond.
3. Calebasse traditionnelle avec bouchon scellé.

pages.title: Ash and Protective Leaves Against Insects
pages.text:
To protect your beans, corn, and cowpeas against weevils without chemicals:
1. **Sieved wood ash**: mix one-third very dry fine ash with two-thirds seeds in the jar. The ash suffocates insects and dries out the air!
2. **Repellent leaves**: add dried neem leaves or dried hot pepper to the container.
Your seeds will remain intact for months!
pages.illustration_description:
Gros plan sur la préparation :
Le maraîcher verse de la cendre de bois très fine et tamisée sur des haricots dans un bocal, puis pose deux piments rouges très secs sur le dessus avant de fermer le couvercle.
Annotation : "100 % naturel et zéro insecte ✅".

pages.title: Accurate Labeling: The Memory of Your Work
pages.text:
A seed without a label is a lost seed!
Affix a paper label to each jar indicating:
1. The name of the vegetable and variety (e.g., *Local Round Tomato*).
2. The harvest location (your field or village).
3. The month and year of harvest (e.g., *March 2026*).
Also, slip a small, identical paper inside the jar in case the outer label comes off.
pages.illustration_description:
Bocal de semences avec une belle étiquette lisible scotchée dessus :
"Piment doux d'hivernage — Parcelle du bas — Récolte Février 2026 — Germination 90%".
Un double du papier est visible à l'intérieur contre la paroi vitrée.

pages.title: Where to store your precious jars?
pages.text:
Always keep your seed containers:
- In the coolest and darkest room of the house (e.g., at the foot of an earthen wall or in a buried clay jar).
- Off the ground to avoid rodents and direct humidity.
- Never put your seeds in the freezer if you have frequent power outages: thawing creates fatal condensation!
pages.illustration_description: Intérieur d'une maison traditionnelle fraîche : une grande jarre en terre cuite posée sur un support surélevé contenant les bocaux hermétiques bien rangés, loin de la fenêtre et du soleil.

pages.title: Congratulations! Your Future Harvests Are in Good Hands
pages.text:
Congratulations! You have mastered the entire seed production chain:
✅ You know how to ferment tomatoes and wash squash seeds
✅ You dry in the shade without burning the germination power
✅ You sort your seeds by winnowing and flotation
✅ You store hermetically with ash and neem
Fundamental Block A is validated! You are ready for the practical vegetable datasheets!
pages.illustration_description: Le maraîcher contemple une belle étagère remplie de bocaux de graines étiquetés et scellés. Les pots rayonnent d'une douce lueur dorée, symbolisant la richesse et l'autonomie paysanne. Grandes coches vertes ✅ et banderole de réussite du socle fondamental.
